canonical_name: Neron-Tate pairing on an elliptic curve
canonical_human_claim: For an elliptic curve E over a number field K, polarization of the Neron-Tate canonical height defines a symmetric bilinear pairing on E(K), with self-pairing equal to the canonical height; it is nonnegative on the diagonal and its diagonal kernel is exactly the torsion subgroup, so it induces a positive-definite pairing on E(K) modulo torsion.
domain_and_universes: K is a number field; E is an elliptic curve over K; P,Q,R range over E(K); m,n range over Int; Lean universes are those required by the selected mathlib model.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Rat
hat_h is the correctly normalized Neron-Tate canonical height
conclusions: the polarization formula defines the pairing
the pairing is symmetric and additive in each argument
self-pairing is zero exactly for torsion points
the induced pairing modulo torsion is positive definite
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: the identity and all torsion points lie in the diagonal kernel
m or n equal to zero and negative integers are included
the number-field hypothesis is not broadened
the factor one-half and canonical-height normalization must be preserved
